newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Suspected Philippine rebel chief said captured.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Philippine rebel chief said captured.

text.p: Philippine Armed Forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera said on Saturday government agents had captured the leader of a Moslem rebel group fighting for an Islamic state in the southern Philippines.
Acedera told reporters he had received a report from the navy that Abdurajak Janjalani, head of the Abu Sayyaf fundamentalist group, was arrested while about to board a ship in central Cebu City.

"I have been informed, but I don't have the formal report yet, that Janjalani has been caught," Acedera said in the northern city of Baguio where he was to attend Sunday's graduation ceremonies at the Philippine Military Academy.
Large amounts of cash were taken from the guerrilla, who was with his family when he was arrested, Acedera said.
He did not say what Janjalani was doing in Cebu, a Christian city where Moslem guerillas do not operate.
There have been several instances in the past when the military has announced the arrest of a rebel leader only to backtrack later after realising it was a case of mistaken identity.
Acedera did not say how the military was able to positively establish the identity of the arrested man.
An obscure preacher until he took up arms, Janjalani has been the object of intensive military manhunt for several years.

The military has blamed the Abu Sayyaf for a spate of bombings and raids on government and religious targets in the southern islands and for the kidnappings of several Filipino and foreign missionaries in the area in the past four years.
